title: Type Narrowing
lead: Narrowing tightens the static type of a binding at a control-flow position. It is semantics, not a diagnostic optimization: narrowed types drive member lookup, overload resolution, match exhaustiveness, and code generation, and the VM and AOT backends must agree. Normative rules N-1..N-13 live in spec section 2.13.

sections.heading: What can be narrowed (N-1, N-2)
sections.markdown:
Only **simple bindings** narrow: local `var` / `const` bindings and bare parameter identifiers.

Never narrowed, even after a null check: `p.f`, `this.f`, `a[i]`, `t.0`, `f()`, and any other non-identifier expression. Extract a local binding first (N-3).

sections.heading: Fact table (N-4)
sections.markdown:
| Condition | True branch | False branch |
|--|--|--|
| `x` | remove `null` | no fact |
| `!e` | false fact of `e` | true fact of `e` |
| `(e)` | true fact of `e` | false fact of `e` |
| `x == null` | keep only `null` | remove `null` |
| `x != null` | remove `null` | keep only `null` |
| `x is T` | intersect with `T` | remove intersection with `T` |
| `typeOf(x) == Type.K` | keep kind `K` | remove kind `K` |
| `e1 && e2` | true facts of both | no fact |
| `e1 \|\| e2` | no fact | false facts of both |

Forms not in the table produce no facts.

For nested Optionals, a null test observes the outer layer of the current read type R. Repeated tests of the same binding prove successive layers. Evidence identifies the binding, declared type, layer and mutation generation; joins retain only a common consecutive prefix. Earlier evidence cannot revive after a write, including in a short-circuit true branch.

sections.heading: Short-circuit inheritance (N-5)
sections.markdown: `T?` cannot be used directly as a condition, so `&&` / `||` inheritance is the standard way to work with nullable values: the right operand of `&&` is analyzed under the left operand's true fact, and the right operand of `||` under its false fact.

sections.heading: Where facts apply (N-7, N-8, N-9, N-10)
sections.markdown: `if` then/else bodies, both arms of `c ? a : b`, loop-body entry and the code after `while` / `for`, the right operand of `&&` / `||`, and the code after `assert(c)`. A branch that necessarily terminates gives the following code the opposite fact.

sections.heading: Invalidation (N-11)
sections.markdown:
Narrowing is invalidated by assignment / compound assignment / `++` / `--`, by passing the binding as a `ref` argument, and by `move`. A binding captured by a closure **and** assigned anywhere never narrows in that function. An ordinary call does not invalidate narrowing, because a narrowable subject cannot be written by a callee.

Resolving a direct ref place does not execute the callee. All value arguments finish before the callee can write; an earlier nested ref call invalidates later reads, while an already evaluated owned SSA value remains valid. An unreachable lazy default has no runtime mutation effect.

sections.heading: Unwrapping and E0379 (N-12, N-13)
sections.markdown:
`E0379` fires when a receiver's static type can still be `null` (including a type that is always `null`) and the program does member access, indexing, a call, arithmetic, or iteration on it.

Nested Optional consumption follows spec section 2.5. A normal read of a simple binding unwraps its proven consecutive Some prefix p, yielding exact read type R and q=p explicit claims. `!` and `??` first consume one available claim without unwrapping or rewrapping R. With no claim, `!` unwraps one current Optional layer and panics on its absence; `??` tests only that layer and evaluates its default only when absent. Groups preserve claims; calls, returns, conversions and new bindings do not inherit old read claims. An unreachable default still undergoes complete type, visibility, construction-authority, generic-constraint and effect checks. Optional chaining follows its separate whole-chain short-circuit contract; its Source admission remains separate.
